title: Trump's stock purchases and Truth Social posts
summary: The Donald J. Trump Revocable Trust holds about 52-53% of TMTG, which owns Truth Social. Trump named a company by its ticker in office (Palantir, 'PLTR', April 10, 2026). OGE filings, including a 113-page Q1 2026 Form 278-T with about 3,600-3,700 trades, show Palantir buys weeks before that post, and the Trump side says independent managers or his children handle the trades. The Intel Oval Office meme is real: Trump posted it in Sept 2025 and again in Sept 2026. It refers to the government's Intel stake, not a personal trade, and nothing shows the post caused any price move. After the 2025 post the stock actually dipped.

sub_claims.statement: TMTG is largely owned by the Donald J. Trump Revocable Trust and owns Truth Social.
sub_claims.finding: In Dec 2024 Trump transferred about 114.75M DJT shares (about 52-53%) to the revocable trust. Trump is the sole beneficiary and Donald Trump Jr. is the trustee. Truth Social is TMTG's platform.

sub_claims.statement: Trump promotes stocks on Truth Social, even naming companies by ticker while in office.
sub_claims.finding: On April 10, 2026, Trump praised Palantir and included '(PLTR)', reported as a first for a sitting president. Shares briefly rose about 3% from intraday lows but closed lower.

sub_claims.statement: Hundreds of pages of financial disclosures show the president bought equities before posting about them.
sub_claims.finding: The Q1 2026 Form 278-T is 113 pages long and lists about 3,642-3,711 trades worth $220M-$750M. A 2025 disclosure listed more than 21,000 trades. It shows $247k-$630k of Palantir buys in Q1 2026, including at least seven in March, before the April 10 post. The filings give only value ranges. Most trades were never followed by a related post, and there is no evidence that Trump directed them.

sub_claims.statement: His office says someone else traded on his behalf, so he couldn't have known.
sub_claims.finding: The Trump Organization says independent third-party managers make all trading decisions with no family input. White House spokesman David Ingle said the assets are in a trust managed by his children and that 'there are no conflicts of interest.' It is not a blind trust: Trump certifies he knows the holdings.

sub_claims.statement: Trump posted a meme of himself trading Intel stock in the Oval Office, and the price went up afterward.
sub_claims.finding: The meme is real. In Sept 2025 an AI image read 'Bought Intel at $20 / Intel now at $30', referring to the US government's 9.9% stake bought at $20.47 a share. Intel slipped after hours and fell more than 2% premarket after that post, and its 23% jump that week came from the Nvidia deal. In Sept 2026 a $20-to-$95 version was followed by a gain of more than 4% overnight within an existing rally. Nothing shows the post caused either move.

corrections: The Intel meme depicts the US government's Intel stake (bought at $20.47 a share in Aug 2025), framed as a gain for the country, not Trump's personal trade.
After the Sept 2025 Intel meme the stock dipped. Only the Sept 2026 repost was followed by a rise, and that rise was already part of a rally.
The 'others trade for him' defense comes mainly from the Trump Organization (independent managers). The White House line is that his children manage the trust.
denials_and_context: Trump Organization: independent third-party managers make all trading decisions with no family input.
White House spokesman David Ingle: the assets are in a trust managed by his children, and 'there are no conflicts of interest.'
Fortune's analysis: the trade pattern looks like direct indexing and tax-loss harvesting. CNN: most trades were never followed by a related post.
Critics (Rep. Don Beyer, NOTUS, CREW): it is not a blind trust, Trump missed STOCK Act deadlines and paid late fees, and Palantir sponsored administration events and donated to the ballroom project.
The disclosures report only value ranges, and the same filing shows a sale of up to $5M of Palantir on Feb 10, 2026.
